{
  "summary": "Adds opt-in CMake/CTest registration for the Python functional test suite and exercises it in the native macOS CI job. When enabled via `-DBUILD_FUNCTIONAL_TESTS=ON`, `test_runner.py` emits an inventory manifest that CTest reads (either via CMake 4.4+'s native `discover_tests()` or a bundled fallback script) to register individual functional tests alongside unit tests, executing each test directly via a new `--ctest-direct` runner mode.",
  "problem": "Functional tests are orchestrated exclusively by `test_runner.py`, preventing developers and CI workflows from using standard CTest commands and flags (`-R`, `-L`, `--rerun-failed`, `--parallel`) to run both unit and functional tests together, and hiding functional test results from CTest-compatible IDEs and downstream tooling.",
  "evidence": [
    "Author description: \"Running the functional tests via CTest lets CI and developers can use the same standard CTest interface to run all unit and enabled functional tests! Individual tests become easy to inspect and rerun with standard CTest features such as -R, -L, --rerun-failed, --output-on-failure, and -j.\"",
    "Author description: \"This also lets functional tests (and their output) become visible to CTest-aware IDEs, CTest dashboards, CDash, and all other downstream tooling that already understands CTest metadata.\""
  ],
  "dependencies": {
    "depends_on": [],
    "enables": []
  },
  "scope_notes": "Includes a CMake-scripted fallback implementation of CMake 4.4's `discover_tests()` (`test/functional/functional_discovery.cmake.in`) generated by an LLM to support older CMake versions.",
  "changed_since_previous": "",
  "card": "Adds opt-in CMake/CTest registration for Python functional tests, allowing developers and CI to run unit and functional tests together using standard CTest invocations and filtering. It introduces manifest-generation and direct-execution modes in test_runner.py, registers tests via CMake 4.4+ discover_tests() or a compatibility shim, and wires the macOS CI job to use it. This addresses the lack of unified test orchestration and integration with CTest-aware IDEs and CI tooling without changing the default local workflow. No dependencies are noted.",

  "confidence": "high",

result.summary: Adds opt-in CMake/CTest registration for the Python functional test suite and exercises it in the native macOS CI job. When enabled via `-DBUILD_FUNCTIONAL_TESTS=ON`, `test_runner.py` emits an inventory manifest that CTest reads (either via CMake 4.4+'s native `discover_tests()` or a bundled fallback script) to register individual functional tests alongside unit tests, executing each test directly via a new `--ctest-direct` runner mode.
result.problem: Functional tests are orchestrated exclusively by `test_runner.py`, preventing developers and CI workflows from using standard CTest commands and flags (`-R`, `-L`, `--rerun-failed`, `--parallel`) to run both unit and functional tests together, and hiding functional test results from CTest-compatible IDEs and downstream tooling.
evidence: Author description: "Running the functional tests via CTest lets CI and developers can use the same standard CTest interface to run all unit and enabled functional tests! Individual tests become easy to inspect and rerun with standard CTest features such as -R, -L, --rerun-failed, --output-on-failure, and -j."

Author description: "This also lets functional tests (and their output) become visible to CTest-aware IDEs, CTest dashboards, CDash, and all other downstream tooling that already understands CTest metadata."
result.scope_notes: Includes a CMake-scripted fallback implementation of CMake 4.4's `discover_tests()` (`test/functional/functional_discovery.cmake.in`) generated by an LLM to support older CMake versions.
result.card: Adds opt-in CMake/CTest registration for Python functional tests, allowing developers and CI to run unit and functional tests together using standard CTest invocations and filtering. It introduces manifest-generation and direct-execution modes in test_runner.py, registers tests via CMake 4.4+ discover_tests() or a compatibility shim, and wires the macOS CI job to use it. This addresses the lack of unified test orchestration and integration with CTest-aware IDEs and CI tooling without changing the default local workflow. No dependencies are noted.
